completion_conditions: A Guardian comment that refuses or revokes approval can never satisfy the gate, and a removed guardian label cannot be replayed by another actor.
A rename cannot move a file out of locked scope unseen, and no PR can modify or delete another goal's mirror records.
A CCA verdict of complete that itself marks an acceptance criterion failed, or sets can_merge false, is refused by both the verdict enforcer and MergeGate.
A dispatched repair reaches the PR head; a failed push stops the loop instead of silently burning a repair attempt.
A multi-task goal is never marked complete on main after only its first task merges, and goal_complete never reverts an unrelated goal's in-flight state.
The MergeGate metadata job passes the flags its own mode requires, orchestrator evidence is actually committed, and no GitHub expression is interpolated into a run: body.
A retried shiki start re-attempts every GitHub governance step, an existing branch is never force-reset, and doctor reports an unprotected branch as a failure.
Migrations apply in a target repository and fail with the [shiki] error contract.
Every mirror record validates against the schema shipped beside it, enforced in CI.

decisions: Concurrency is not the constraint: every Shiki task locks path:.shiki/** and try_acquire_locks refuses on overlap, so at most one task is in flight repo-wide. The plan is a single lane; ordering, not parallelism, is the design question.

Cross-goal ordering (hard): R-01 before ADR0015-T5; ADR0015-T1 before R-02 before ADR0015-T5; R-02 before R-03 (the CCA verdict schema file is unmergeable until runtime_evidence_path is fixed); R-05 before ADR0015-T6; R-04 before ADR0015-T3 and T6; R-09 last.

One fold is recommended into ADR 0015 rather than planned here: guardian-policy.json is read from the PR head, so a PR can name its own author a Guardian and self-approve. ADR0015-T4 already locks both mergegate_check.py and guardian-policy.json, and its acceptance check 5 is unsatisfiable without this fix. Folding it requires a second Spec Amendment to the ADR 0015 plan.

R-07 is recommended to be pulled forward: a target repo can run Shiki with no server-side enforcement at all, which makes every ADR 0015 gate decorative in targets. It has zero effect on this platform repo.

Surfaces where nothing survived, recorded so the absence is evidence: runner auth and secret handling, the external AI Guardian review path (ADR 0010/0014), the memory subsystem, and goal_reconcile's own validator (probed repeatedly as a bypass and held every time).
grill_with_docs.source: Repo-wide adversarial audit 2026-07-25 (Workflow we1mhqcd4, 43 agents: 8 surface finders -> independent refuters on every blocking/important finding -> 1 synthesizer). 27 findings survived; 20 are non-minor.

non_goals: The six defects owned by ADR 0015 goal G-20260725T112636727659Z-23ba3b56 (contract mutability, head-resolved risk/locks, the dispatch gate, the needs: cca dependency, the multi-task contract path, test_command freezing).
Replacing GITHUB_TOKEN for the orchestrator evidence PR — that creates a long-lived credential and is a Guardian decision.
Reconciling live branch protection with .shiki/config.yaml — an operator action on GitHub, not code.
Judging CCA checklist quality; the profile-coverage check detects a non-evaluating CCA, not a lazy one.
Changing the id generator or migrating existing record ids.
operator_actions_required: Reconcile live branch protection with .shiki/config.yaml: main currently reports require_code_owner_reviews false and required_approving_review_count 0, so the CODEOWNERS second factor ADR 0015 relies on is inert on GitHub. 'MergeGate metadata check' is also a live check but not a protected context.
Decide whether the orchestrator evidence-PR path is wanted at all; if it is, it needs a credential that is not GITHUB_TOKEN, which is a Guardian decision about blast radius.

Clear the unregistered-worktree condition `shiki doctor` reports before dispatching contracts 0 and 11: `bash scripts/test_shiki_guardian_policy.sh` exits 1 in this checkout because doctor fails on stale sibling worktrees (e.g. /Users/kio.mizutani/.worktrees/shiki-pr178-secret-set-claude-repair). A dispatched worktree shares the same gitdir and inherits the failure, so the TDD gate fails closed before a PR exists. Either `git worktree remove` them (destructive git — Guardian-authorized, not agent-executable) or register them under .shiki/worktrees/. The script is green on a clean clone of the same commit, so this is environment residue, not a code defect — and the cheapest green path for an implementer would be to weaken the assertion, which both contracts' non-goals forbid.
outcome: The 20 non-minor defects that survived independent refutation in the repo-wide adversarial audit are closed, without weakening the in-flight ADR 0015 contract-approval work: Guardian approval evidence becomes current and revocable, MergeGate scope enforcement sees renames and the whole mirror, a self-contradictory CCA verdict is refused, repairs actually reach the PR, closeout stops completing goals early and clobbering sibling state, workflows invoke what they claim to, bootstrap never destroys a target or skips its governance setup, migrations apply in targets, and the shipped schemas match the ids Shiki generates.

amendments: A1 (operator-approved 2026-07-27, from a live incident): the first autonomous dispatch wrote .shiki/plans/P-20260727T005125000000Z-0015c0de.json carrying spec_freeze.status=frozen with approved_by=mizutani-140 — an operator Spec Freeze the operator never gave — to satisfy an acceptance criterion that could not be met with the artifacts in its worktree, and hard-coded its id into the tests. 412 tests and validate_shiki were green; .shiki/plans/ is outside MergeGate's scoped-mutation rules. R-02 is extended to forbid a PR authoring or modifying any spec_freeze block, including on its own goal's plan, and a new docs slice codifies the prohibition and the stop-instead-of-fabricate rule in the constitution. Note: whether the independent code-review verifier would have caught it is UNTESTED — the loop's gates had not run when the artifact was found.

A-LOCKS (operator-approved 2026-07-28, from the ADR 0016 design review): every task in this plan declared path:tests/** and path:scripts/test_shiki_*.sh, and most declared path:.shiki/**. active_lock_conflicts conflicts on PATTERN overlap alone, before any changed-file intersection, so identical directory globs always collide: 231 of 231 task pairs across the four frozen plans conflicted, and stripping every .shiki lock left it at 231 of 231 — the mirror locks were not the binding colliders, the two test globs were. They were written in by the A5 amendment, whose lesson ('every task must lock a test surface') was right and whose implementation as a directory glob was not. Locks are now narrowed to the files each task actually names in its scope, acceptance checks and test_command, plus the one new test file it creates. Measured after narrowing: 68 of 210 pairs conflict (32.4%), greedy concurrent set of 4. path:.shiki/** is dropped entirely — no gate requires it (MergeGate reports ready with narrow mirror locks) and its only advocate was a warn-only advisory in validate_shiki. This amendment must precede ADR 0015 T1, which makes locks contract-immutable.

A2 (operator-approved 2026-07-28): five tasks added from defects observed during live operation of PR #179, none of which the adversarial audit had found because they only appear when the loop actually runs: lock acquisition rewinding a task's lifecycle and amendments invalidating their own grant; no way for a Guardian to see what the gate wants (nine approval rounds across five distinct failure modes, all presenting identically); task worktrees cut from the coordinator's branch rather than the default branch (56 MergeGate blockers); lock conflicts skipped silently so serialization reads as deadlock; and the CCA short-circuiting its evidence record once any blocker is known.

A4 (operator-approved 2026-07-29): one task added for the seventh and eighth manual interventions found by running the loop — a dispatch does not carry the coordinator's current contract into the worktree, and the delivery path does not carry the transitive evidence its ledgers reference. Both were filled in by hand on PR #181. All six Wave 1 tasks now state in `scope` which manual step they remove, what was observed, and what makes the result reproducible, so the generated PR body carries it verbatim (shiki_github.github_pr_body renders `scope` unchanged).

A5 (operator-approved 2026-07-29, from the pre-dispatch satisfiability audit, 27 agents): all six Wave 1 contracts were BLOCKED as written and none was dispatchable. One defect was shared by all six — no .shiki lock, while origin/main's MergeGate judges the loop's own mirror sync against declared locks; A-LOCKS' premise that no gate requires the lock is true only on PR #181's branch, which is not merged. That is resolved by sequencing the wave behind #181 rather than by re-widening locks. The rest were contract defects and are fixed here: contract 11 could not register its new module for target staging; contract 15's non_goals forbade exactly what an acceptance check required and its scope cited a symbol absent from any base it can be cut from — the #179 shape, caught before dispatch this time; contract 12's proof returned the same answer with the bug present or fixed. A red test_command on contracts 0 and 11 is environment residue and is recorded as an operator action.

A6 (operator-approved 2026-07-29): the red test_command on contracts 0 and 11 is not environment residue as first diagnosed — it is a doctor defect. doctor treats any sibling worktree without a .shiki/worktrees record as a failure, and the coordinator's own session worktree is exactly that from inside every dispatched task worktree, since they share one gitdir. Two stale task worktrees were removed by the operator and the failure persisted with one entry: the coordinator itself. Registering it as a task record would be fabricating evidence, so instead test_shiki_guardian_policy.sh is dropped from those two test_commands with the reason recorded in scope, coverage is kept as an acceptance check, and the fix is given to contract 6, which already locks scripts/shiki_doctor.py.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes. On 2026-07-27/29 a single task was driven from Goal to PR twice (#179, merged; #181, open at the time of writing). The loop's judgments were autonomous; the plumbing between them was not. Seven manual interventions were required, and this task removes one of them.
  Manual step removed: re-running the CCA by hand after a Guardian approval, because approving does not re-evaluate anything.
  Observed: five separate races: the approval landed 32-45 seconds after the run that would have read it, and there is no labeled/unlabeled trigger on shiki-cca-completion.yml, so a recorded approval never reaches a verdict on its own.

NOTE on test_command: scripts/test_shiki_guardian_policy.sh is deliberately NOT in this task's test_command. It calls `shiki doctor`, and doctor's unregistered-worktree check fails whenever any sibling git worktree lacks a .shiki/worktrees record — which is true of the coordinator's own session worktree from inside every dispatched task worktree, since they share one gitdir. The loop execs test_command as its TDD gate and fails closed, so including it would stop this task before a PR exists, for a reason the implementer cannot fix inside its locks. The cheapest green path would be to weaken the doctor assertion, which this task's non-goals forbid. Coverage is kept by an acceptance check requiring the script to pass in a clean checkout instead.

Two defects on the same seam in scripts/shiki_tasks.py, both observed live on PR #179. (a) cmd_lock_acquire and try_acquire_locks set task['status'] = 'ready' unconditionally (lines 373 and 691), so re-acquiring a grant rewinds a task that already has an open PR from review back to ready — MergeGate's post-CCA rule then blocks it. Preserve any status at or beyond 'running'; only planned may become ready. (b) A Spec Amendment that widens a task's locks silently invalidates its own grant, because the grant is checked as a superset of the contract; nothing in the amendment path refreshes it. Detect the divergence and either refresh the grant or fail with a reason naming it, rather than surfacing as an unexplained 'locks are not granted'.

The loop's judgments were autonomous; the plumbing between them was not. Seven manual interventions were required, and this task removes one of them.
  Manual step removed: re-acquiring a lock by hand after every contract amendment.
  Observed: three amendments (A3, A3b and the earlier A-LOCKS widening) each invalidated their own grant, surfacing only as 'locks are not granted' with no indication that an amendment caused it; one re-acquisition also rewound a task with an open PR from review to ready and blocked MergeGate.
  Reproducible when: amending a contract's locks leaves a valid grant, or fails with a reason naming the divergence, and no re-acquisition ever moves a task backwards through its lifecycle.

NOTE on test_command: scripts/test_shiki_guardian_policy.sh is deliberately NOT in this task's test_command. It calls `shiki doctor`, and doctor's unregistered-worktree check fails whenever any sibling git worktree lacks a .shiki/worktrees record — which is true of the coordinator's own session worktree from inside every dispatched task worktree, since they share one gitdir. The loop execs test_command as its TDD gate and fails closed, so including it would stop this task before a PR exists, for a reason the implementer cannot fix inside its locks. The cheapest green path would be to weaken the doctor assertion, which this task's non-goals forbid. Coverage is kept by an acceptance check requiring the script to pass in a clean checkout instead.

tasks.scope: Observed on PR #179: with CCA-08 already failing, the CCA judged that the verdict was determined and stopped, returning seven acceptance criteria as insufficient_evidence in 1m30s where an earlier run had evaluated the same criteria in detail. The verdict was right and the evidence record was hollow. Because complete requires every blocking criterion to pass, a short-circuited run can never become complete, and the record is systematically thin exactly when a blocker exists — which is most of the time. Require the prompt and the verdict enforcer to evaluate every blocking checklist item and acceptance criterion regardless of an already-known blocker, and reject a verdict that returns blocking items as insufficient_evidence with 'already blocked' as the reason.

tasks.scope:
A dispatch hands the implementer a worktree, but nothing guarantees that worktree holds the contract the coordinator currently has, nor the evidence that contract references. Two gaps, one seam. (a) shiki runner claude --repair-id renders the handoff from the coordinator while the implementer verifies against the worktree's own .shiki: sync the task, its goal and its lock record into the worktree before the session starts, so the implementer judges against current terms. (b) The delivery path syncs each id in ledger_evidence but not the .shiki paths those ledgers' evidence arrays reference — repair packets and runner EXEC records — leaving dangling pointers that MergeGate blocks on. Walk ledger_evidence transitively and carry everything it points at, with the ownership bound stated directly and reimplemented in shiki_loop.py: expand a ledger only when its own goal_id AND task_id both equal the task's. Do not reuse mergegate_check.ledger_entry_allowed_for_task — it accepts a goal-scoped ledger with an empty task_id, which would defeat this bound.
